title: Grateful Dead Live at Curtis Hixon Convention Hall on 1973-12-19
source: Matrix from sources: soundboard:  97361; and Dan McDonald's audience tape (new flat transfer)

ai_review.summary: A stellar matrix capture of a late‑1973 show highlighted by a soaring Here Comes Sunshine and an earth‑shaking Other One jam, with generally excellent sound despite a few uneven moments.
ai_review.review: The Dusborne/Droncit MTX delivers clear, well‑balanced audio that lets the band’s late‑’73 brilliance shine through. Reviewers rave about the apex version of “Here Comes Sunshine,” the massive “He’s Gone > Truckin’ > The Other One” sequence and Phil’s experimental bass excursions, while noting slower or sloppy spots in songs like “Sugaree,” “Candyman,” and “Around & Around.” Overall the performance is a high‑water mark for the period, captured with solid technical quality.

ai_rating.rationale: Three detailed reviews (two 5‑star, one 4‑star) praise both the musical peaks and the matrix recording’s clarity; minor song‑level criticisms keep the rating just below top‑tier.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with full band balance; no major dropouts reported. Reviewers note it captures the completeness of the show while sounding close to a soundboard.

standout_songs: He’s Gone > Truckin’ > The Other One
Mississippi Half‑Step > Me and Bobby McGee
show_quality.setlist_flow: An uneven first set with a few mid‑tempo stumbles gives way to a powerful second set; the band builds momentum through tight blues numbers and culminates in an intense, speaker‑destroying jam that defines this era.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Delivers soaring wah‑heavy solo on “Candyman,” crystalline slide work on “Row Jimmy,” and magical phrasing on “Stella Blue.”
band_member_comments.Phil: Shows his experimental side with a noisy bass jam, low‑frequency explosions, and the rare ‘Decon Jam’ that pushes the PA as an instrument.
band_member_comments.Bob: Strong vocal presence on “The Other One” verse but criticized for over‑the‑top screaming on “Around & Around.”
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboards are energetic—prickly chords, bluesy tritone stingers, and inspired fills on “El Paso,” “Ramble On Rose,” and the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s snare shines on “Big Railroad Blues” and “Big River,” driving the band forward with crisp, punchy rhythms.
